title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X/S is a smooth curve and ω = Ω^1_{X/S}. P^1_{X/S}(ω) is the rank-2 bundle of first-order principal parts of ω, with exact sequence 0 → ω⊗Ω^1 = ω^2 → P^1(ω) → ω → 0, so det P^1(ω) ≅ ω^3.

Objects. P is the P^1-bundle of rank-1 quotients of P^1(ω), in Grothendieck's convention. σ is the canonical section given by the quotient P^1(ω) → ω. 𝒯 = Isom(P^1_X, P) is the associated PGL_2-torsor, with Borel B and unipotent radical B_u ≅ G_a. Then 𝒯/B = P, and 𝒯/B_u → P is a G_m-torsor. A projective connection c_0 is a connection on 𝒯 (equivalently on P) satisfying the usual transversality with respect to σ.

1. Identifying 𝒯/B_u. Grothendieck identifies 𝒯/B_u over P with the G_m-torsor of nowhere-vanishing sections of Ω^1_{P/X}. He also calls these 'structures de courbe projective d'indice 1'. A point of 𝒯/B_u over a section σ' of P is a pair:
- a quotient line bundle L of P^1(ω), i.e. a first-order differential operator D: ω → L that generates L;
- a trivialisation of the vertical cotangent line at that point.
With N = Ker(P^1(ω) → L) one has Ω^1_{P/X}|σ' = N⊗L^{-1} ≅ ω^3⊗L^{-2}. So the second datum is an isomorphism φ: L^2 ≅ ω^3, i.e. L is a 'square root of ω^3'.

2. Sections disjoint from σ. If σ' is disjoint from σ, the symbol ω^2 → L is an isomorphism. Then D is a connection D: ω → ω⊗Ω^1 = ω^2, and the extra datum reduces to a nowhere-vanishing section φ of ω.

3. Horizontality. For the induced connection, such a section of 𝒯/B_u is horizontal iff Dφ = 0.

4. Developing maps. The sheaf 𝒰 of horizontal sections of 𝒯 is the sheaf of germs of étale maps t: X^an → P^1(C) with t^*(c) = c_0, where c is the unique canonical projective structure on P^1. One has t^*(c) = c_{D_t}, where D_t is the connection on ω for which dt is horizontal.

5. Affine charts. For an étale s: X^an → E^1(C) = A^1, s^*(D_can) = D_s, where D_can is the canonical connection on Ω^1_{A^1} with dT horizontal. To realise a given connection D as D_s:
- write D = D_t + ϖ, with ϖ ∈ Γ(ω), using a local coordinate t;
- compute D_s = D_t + s'·d(1/s') = D_t − ds'/s', where s' = ds/dt;
- so the equation is −d log s' = ϖ.

6. Solutions (next page). With ϖ = λ dt this gives s''/s' = −λ, so s = c∫exp(−Λ) + c'. The solutions form a torsor under the affine group Aut(A^1).

Overall picture. The chain 𝒯 → 𝒯/B_u → 𝒯/B, t ↦ (D_t, dt) ↦ D_t, matches three levels of local structure:
- projective charts (sections of 𝒯);
- pairs of an affine structure and a parallel 1-form, i.e. translation-type charts (sections of 𝒯/B_u);
- affine structures compatible with c_0 (sections of P disjoint from σ).
The purpose is to understand the horizontal (analytic, transcendental) sections of the projective-connection bundle, within the Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs study of second-order equations on curves.
errors: Minor: in the disjoint case the transcription says 'trivialisation φ de ω^2'. From L ≅ ω^2 and L^2 ≅ ω^3 the datum is really a trivialisation of ω, i.e. a nowhere-vanishing φ ∈ Γ(ω), which agrees with the next page ('φ ne s'annulant pas').
The text says 'regarder les t telles que D = D_s'; it should read 's'. This is a slip of notation.
Otherwise the computation D_s = D_t − ds'/s' and the identification of Ω^1_{P/X} along a section with ω^3⊗L^{-2} are correct, with P parametrising quotients in Grothendieck's convention.

ideas.what: PGL_2-torsor 𝒯 of a projective connection, with quotients 𝒯/B = P and 𝒯/B_u = G_m-torsor of Ω^1_{P/X}; horizontal sections of the three levels correspond to projective charts, (affine connection, parallel 1-form) pairs, and affine structures
ideas.modern_name: Opers / (G,X)-structures; reductions of a PGL_2-oper to B and B_u
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1960s) for projective and affine structures on Riemann surfaces; Beilinson–Drinfeld (1990s) for opers

ideas.what: Sections of P disjoint from the canonical section σ correspond to connections D on ω (affine structures) with c_D = c_0
ideas.modern_name: Affine structures subordinate to a projective structure; Riccati equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Gunning; Deligne, Équations différentielles à points singuliers réguliers, 1970)

ideas.what: A section of 𝒯/B_u over a section of P is a quotient L of P^1(ω) together with L^2 ≅ ω^3 ('racine carrée de ω^3')
ideas.modern_name: Vertical cotangent of the oper P^1-bundle; link to theta characteristics / SL_2 lifts

ideas.what: Developing equation for affine charts: D = D_t + ϖ, D_s = D_t − d log s', so s''/s' = −λ and s = c∫exp(−Λ) + c'
ideas.modern_name: Developing map of an affine structure

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, self-made re-derivation of the standard hierarchy projective → affine → translation structures on a curve, phrased through the torsors 𝒯 → 𝒯/B_u → 𝒯/B. That is essentially the B-reduction picture of opers, anticipating the Beilinson–Drinfeld language, but the content is classical and routine. The 'L^2 ≅ ω^3' remark is a nice detail, but it is standard.
transcription_corrections: 'Le fibré Π/B_n un P' should read 'Le fibré 𝒯/B_u sur P'.
'N⊗L^{-1} ≃ L^{-2}⊗ω' should read 'N⊗L^{-1} ≃ L^{-2}⊗ω^3', consistent with the stated φ: L^2 ≃ ω^3.
'trivialisation φ de ω^2' is most likely 'trivialisation φ de ω' (φ ∈ Γ(ω)).
'P^1_E(C)' / 'E^1(C)' denotes the affine line 𝔼^1(C) ⊂ P^1(C).
'regarder les t telles que D = D_s' should read 'les s telles que D = D_s'.
'(ϖ ∈ Γ(ω))' should read 'ϖ ∈ Γ(ω_)' with ω underlined; the first-line '(D, λ)' is '(D, φ)'.
